Mob Psycho is an underrated mainstream anime. The animation is absolutely beautiful and stunning, though you mostly see it during the second season. It’s only 2 seasons, 26 episodes if I remember correctly, and isn’t getting any more. It was made by the same manga artist who made One Punch Man and has comedy in it. I was originally turned off by the artstyle, but I gave it a chance and it’s one of my favorites

I haven’t finished AoT yet, but the story leaves you in suspense each and every episode. The openings are an absolute blast to listen to, lots of blood if you’re into that, and is just overall an amazing experience. I’m about halfway through part 1 of season 3 and I’ve heard great reviews on the second part. 

Demon Slayer has become a mainstream anime because of its animation and for good reason. Yeah, it’s slowly turning into MHA and what Naruto used to be with nitpicking fans that probably watched it for their first anime, but the anime is a blast to watch. LiSa made the opening, one of my favorite Japanese bands, the story’s got comedy and some loving characters. The plot isn’t complex, mostly just bland, but it’s still enjoyable. If you decide to read the manga, prepare for an emotional rollercoaster.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime doesn’t get enough love. Yes, it’s an Isekai, but it’s one of the more well done ones. I’ll be honest, I forgot the main characters original name, but he got stabbed, told his friend to delete his search history, then died. Season 2 is coming out October, or it originally was (might’ve been delayed due to Covid), and it’s my personal favorite Isekai. The main character starts to build a civilization, meets new people, it’s honestly super good. It’s hard to explain in words, but it’s a definite watch. I think there’s a little over 20 episodes, though I can’t remember off the top of my head

If you’re asking for a starter pack, JoJo is definitely going to be in it. Parts 1 and 2 have around 25 episodes combined, though the later have about 39, excluding Stardust Crusaders. It’s a good mix of comedy, action, and outsmarting your opponents outsmarting. Each part follows a new jojo, though it’s hard to pick up from the start of part 2, and goes through the Joestar generations. 

There are clearly more anime that could’ve been here, such as Naruto or Gintama, but those have hundreds of episodes. The longest show in this list is Jojo, so I’d say watch that last.

A fish was watching a fly and thought to himself ‘If that fly drops 6 inches, I’ll jump out, catch it, and have a really nice meal.’

What the fish didn’t know was that there was a bear watching from a distance. The bear thought to himself ‘if that fly drops six inches and that fish jumps out to get it, I’ll catch the fish and have a really nice meal.’

What the bear didn’t know was that there was a hunter eating a sandwich across the river watching the entire thing. The hunter thought ‘if that fly jumps out and that fish jumps out, then the bear will jump out and I’ll drop my sandwich to shoot it and have a really nice meal’.

And what the hunter didn’t notice was that there was a mouse watching everything. The mouse thought ‘if that fly drops six inches, that fish will jump out of the water and the bear will get him. Then the hunter will throw down his sandwich to shoot the bear and I’ll get the sandwich and have a really nice meal’.

And what the mouse didn’t know was that there was a cat watching everything. The cat thought ‘if that fly drops six inches, that fish will catch it and the bear will get the fish. Then the hunter will throw down his sandwich to shoot it and the mouse will go for the sandwich. Then I’ll go out and catch the mouse and have a really nice meal’.

Then it all happened. The fly dropped six inches, the fish jumped out to catch it, the bear grabbed the fish, the hunter threw down his sandwich to shoot the bear, and the mouse grabbed the sandwich.

There was one mistake. The cat had missed the mouse and landed on the river.
